Simulating from saved fits

  • Show All Code
  • Hide All Code
On this page

On this page

  • Prepare the environment and inputs

Use this procedure when you already have fitted parameters and want new simulated responses. It reconstructs the saved models, assigns parameters to the appropriate participants, and writes response files that any compatible analysis template can read. No optimization is performed.

You need the observations describing the experimental lists and saved fit records for those observations. The supplied files demonstrate the workflow; your own named fits and response output folders can replace them.

For input conventions, see the data guide.

Configure this run

Replace fit_paths with the named paths printed by your fitting run. A value may also be a directory of compatible participant-fit JSON files; that directory must contain only records for that model and no duplicate participants. Keep model_labels keyed by the same names.

Choose experiment_count, simulation_seed and the observation selection. Repetitions generate more responses from the same participants; they do not add independent participants. Set simulation_dir explicitly for your run: its supplied default is separate from output_dir. With redo_sims=False, matching responses can be reused; missing or incompatible responses are generated.

Keep all editable settings in this tagged cell. Later cells derive paths and selections after any Papermill overrides.

1 — Configure the saved fits and simulation work unit 
# Inputs and saved results — change these for your project.
project_root = None  # Explicit folder, enclosing Git root, or current directory.
data_path = "data/Dupertuys2026.h5"
output_dir = "results/simulation"

# Models and saved fits — names connect specifications, labels and outputs.
fit_paths = {
    "CMR": "data/fits/Dupertuys2026_CMR_demo.json",
    "eCMR_source_only": "data/fits/Dupertuys2026_eCMR_source_only.json",
    "eCMR_broad": "data/fits/Dupertuys2026_eCMR_broad.json",
}
model_labels = {
    "CMR": "CMR",
    "eCMR_source_only": "Source-only eCMR",
    "eCMR_broad": "Broader eCMR",
}

# Observation selection — queries use fields in your dataset.
trial_query = None
max_subjects = 0  # Zero keeps all participants; a positive value selects the first IDs.
subject_indices = []

# Fitting and simulation — optimizer controls are separate from model parameters.
sim_alg_path = None  # Override the recorded simulator, or supply it for older fits.
experiment_count = 10
simulation_seed = 1
redo_sims = True
enable_x64 = True

# Uncertainty and optional behavioral summaries.
confidence_level = 0.95
plot_seed = 0
comparison_analysis_configs = [
    {"target": "jaxcmr.analyses.spc.plot_spc", "title": "Recall by study position"},
    {
        "target": "jaxcmr.analyses.pnr.plot_pnr",
        "title": "First recall",
        "kwargs": {"query_recall_position": 0},
    },
    {
        "target": "jaxcmr.analyses.crp.plot_crp",
        "title": "Temporal transitions",
        "kwargs": {"max_lag": 5},
    },
    {
        "target": "jaxcmr.analyses.cat_recall_rate.plot_cat_recall_rate",
        "title": "Category recall within mixed lists",
        "contrast_name": "Item category",
        "trial_query": "data['list_type'] == 1",
        "kwargs": {
            "category_field": "valence",
            "category_values": [-1, 0],
            "category_labels": ["Emotional", "Neutral"],
            "valid_field": "pres_itemnos",
        },
    },
]
single_analysis_configs = []
analysis_trial_query = "jnp.all(data['pres_itemnos'] > 0, 1)"
filter_repeated_recalls = False
redo_figures = True

# Output overrides and appearance — None uses the default location or style.
simulation_dir = "results/simulations"
figure_dir = None
figure_str = "model_and_data"  # Empty displays figures without saving.
figure_formats = ["png"]
figure_size = (10, 4.8)

Prepare the environment and inputs

Run the following setup cells once, then continue in order. The short installation cell runs only in Colab; local and Slurm runs use the environment you selected during Setup.

project_root anchors relative paths. When it is unset, Colab uses the current directory; elsewhere the notebook uses the enclosing Git project if present, or the current directory. Check the printed location. copy_example_inputs copies requested bundled examples there, reuses matching files, and refuses to overwrite conflicting files. Custom input paths remain your responsibility.

3 — Import packages 
import json

import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpy as np

import jaxcmr
from jaxcmr import repetition
from jaxcmr.examples import copy_example_inputs
from jaxcmr.models import model_factory_from_paths
from jaxcmr.fitting import combine_participant_parameters, parameters_for_subjects
from jaxcmr.dataset import generate_trial_mask
from jaxcmr.helpers import import_from_string
from jaxcmr.helpers import load_data, save_dict_to_hdf5
from jaxcmr.helpers import resolve_project_path, resolve_project_root
from jaxcmr.plotting import save_figure
from jaxcmr.plotting import iter_analysis_figures
from jaxcmr.simulation import (
    load_matching_simulation,
    simulate_dataset,
)

Feature composition stays explicit here. feature_column selects the categorical feature, and concat_features=True combines categorical columns before semantic columns. This simulation loader uses the available feature array when only one is supplied.

4 — Define feature loading and model construction 
def load_features(spec):
    semantic = np.load(resolve_project_path(spec["embedding_path"], root_path)) if spec.get("embedding_path") else None
    categorical = (
        np.load(resolve_project_path(spec["emotion_feature_path"], root_path))[
            :,
            int(spec.get("feature_column", 6)) : int(spec.get("feature_column", 6)) + 1,
        ]
        if spec.get("emotion_feature_path")
        else None
    )
    if (
        spec.get("concat_features", False)
        and categorical is not None
        and semantic is not None
    ):
        return np.concatenate([categorical, semantic], axis=1)
    return categorical if categorical is not None else semantic


def construct_model(spec):
    return model_factory_from_paths(spec["model_factory"], spec["components"])
5 — Load observations and establish runtime settings 
root_path = resolve_project_root(project_root)
print("Project directory:", root_path)

copy_example_inputs([data_path, *fit_paths.values()], base_dir=root_path)

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", enable_x64)
data_path = resolve_project_path(data_path, root_path)
output_dir = resolve_project_path(output_dir, root_path)
output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
data = load_data(str(data_path))
data_source = (
    data_path.relative_to(root_path).as_posix()
    if data_path.is_relative_to(root_path)
    else str(data_path)
)
subjects = np.asarray(data["subject"]).ravel()
6 — Define participant-fit compatibility checks 
def check_participant_fit(
    participant_record,
    reference_record,
    specification_keys,
    model_name,
):
    """Reject incompatible model specifications and pooled records."""
    if any(
        participant_record.get(key) != reference_record.get(key)
        for key in specification_keys
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{model_name}: participant fits have incompatible model or input specifications."
        )
    participant_ids = participant_record["fits"]["subject"]
    if participant_record.get("pooled", False) or -1 in participant_ids:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{model_name}: directories must contain participant fits, not pooled fits."
        )
7 — Define participant-file combination 
def combine_participant_fits(participant_records, data, model_name):
    """Combine compatible participant estimates without losing their identities."""
    subjects = np.asarray(data["subject"]).ravel()
    specification_keys = (
        "model_factory",
        "components",
        "simulation_function",
        "loss_function",
        "data_path",
        "fixed",
        "free",
        "embedding_path",
        "emotion_feature_path",
        "feature_column",
        "concat_features",
    )
    reference_record = participant_records[0]
    combined_parameters = combine_participant_parameters(
        [record["fits"] for record in participant_records]
    )
    selected_rows = set()
    for participant_record in participant_records:
        check_participant_fit(
            participant_record,
            reference_record,
            specification_keys,
            model_name,
        )
        participant_ids = participant_record["fits"]["subject"]
        if "selected_trial_indices" in participant_record:
            rows = participant_record["selected_trial_indices"]
            if not np.isin(subjects[rows], participant_ids).all():
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{model_name}: recorded observation rows belong to another participant."
                )
        else:
            mask = generate_trial_mask(
                data,
                participant_record.get(
                    "trial_query", participant_record.get("data_query")
                ),
            )
            rows = np.flatnonzero(
                np.asarray(mask) & np.isin(subjects, participant_ids)
            ).tolist()
        selected_rows.update(rows)
    combined_record = {
        key: reference_record[key]
        for key in specification_keys
        if key in reference_record
    }
    combined_record.update(
        name=model_name,
        label=reference_record.get("label", model_name),
        pooled=False,
        fits=combined_parameters,
        selected_trial_indices=sorted(selected_rows),
    )
    # Preserve boolean settings as recorded before the fitter's numeric conversion.
    combined_record["fixed"] = (
        reference_record.get("fit_configuration", {})
        .get("parameters", {})
        .get("fixed", reference_record["fixed"])
    )
    return combined_record

Reconstruct and check the saved models

The fit records supply model components, parameter values and observation selections. A pooled record assigns one parameter set across selected participants. A directory of participant records is checked for compatible specifications and nonoverlapping IDs, then its parameter rows are combined in participant order.

The checks preserve the relationship between parameters and observations. Selecting another participant is not a way to transfer someone else’s fitted parameters. Inspect the reported selection and paths before generating responses.

9 — Read named fit files or participant-fit directories 
fit_paths = {model_name: resolve_project_path(path, root_path) for model_name, path in fit_paths.items()}
records = {}
for model_name, path in fit_paths.items():
    if not path.is_dir():
        records[model_name] = json.loads(path.read_text())
        continue
    participant_records = [
        json.loads(file.read_text()) for file in sorted(path.glob("*.json"))
    ]
    if not participant_records:
        raise ValueError(f"{model_name}: no participant-fit JSON files in {path}.")
    if sim_alg_path is not None:
        for participant_record in participant_records:
            participant_record["simulation_function"] = sim_alg_path
    records[model_name] = combine_participant_fits(
        participant_records, data, model_name
    )
    print(
        model_name,
        "— combined",
        len(participant_records),
        "files for",
        len(records[model_name]["fits"]["subject"]),
        "participants",
    )
if not records:
    raise ValueError("Supply at least one saved fit.")
display_labels = {
    model_name: model_labels.get(model_name, record.get("label", model_name))
    for model_name, record in records.items()
}
10 — Select matching observations for each fit 
selections = {}
for name, record in records.items():
    if sim_alg_path is not None:
        record["simulation_function"] = sim_alg_path
    if "simulation_function" not in record:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{name}: supply sim_alg_path for a fit without a recorded simulator."
        )
    if record.get("data_path", data_source) != data_source:
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: the fit refers to a different observation file.")
    if trial_query is None and "selected_trial_indices" in record:
        mask = (
            jnp.zeros(len(subjects), dtype=bool)
            .at[jnp.asarray(record["selected_trial_indices"], dtype=int)]
            .set(True)
        )
    else:
        mask = generate_trial_mask(
            data,
            trial_query
            if trial_query is not None
            else record.get("trial_query", record.get("data_query")),
        )
    subject_ids = np.unique(subjects)
    if max_subjects:
        subject_ids = subject_ids[:max_subjects]
    if subject_indices:
        subject_ids = subject_ids[np.asarray(subject_indices, dtype=int)]
    mask &= jnp.isin(data["subject"].ravel(), subject_ids)
    if not record.get("pooled", record["fits"]["subject"] == [-1]):
        mask &= jnp.isin(
            data["subject"].ravel(), jnp.asarray(record["fits"]["subject"])
        )
    if not bool(mask.any()):
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: no observations match the selected work unit.")
    selections[name] = mask
    print(display_labels[name], "—", int(mask.sum()), "lists; fit:", fit_paths[name])
comparison_mask = jnp.logical_or.reduce(jnp.stack(list(selections.values())), axis=0)
11 — Prepare response and figure paths 
simulation_dir = resolve_project_path(simulation_dir, root_path) if simulation_dir is not None else output_dir
figure_dir = resolve_project_path(figure_dir, root_path) if figure_dir is not None else output_dir
figure_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
simulation_paths = {
    name: simulation_dir / f"{record['name']}.h5" for name, record in records.items()
}
if len(set(simulation_paths.values())) != len(simulation_paths):
    raise ValueError("Fit records need distinct names for saved response files.")

Generate and save responses

Each repetition uses the selected experimental lists and keeps the original participant identity. simulation_seed controls random sampling; changing it asks for another realization of the same configured model.

The supplied fits use a simulator that forces observed recall lengths. Agreement in total recall or stopping is consequently imposed. To use a different simulator, set sim_alg_path and check that it answers your intended question. Saved responses have a JSON file of simulation settings; both files are used when checking whether a previous simulation can be reused.

With redo_sims=False, matching settings allow saved responses to be reused. Changes to data or model code in place are not detected: set redo_sims=True after those changes.

12 — Prepare participant parameters and simulation settings 
simulation_inputs = {}
for model_name, fit_record in records.items():
    model_factory = construct_model(fit_record)
    features = load_features(fit_record)
    selected_trials = selections[model_name]
    is_pooled = fit_record.get("pooled", fit_record["fits"]["subject"] == [-1])
    participant_ids = jnp.unique(data["subject"].ravel()[selected_trials])
    subject_parameters = parameters_for_subjects(fit_record, participant_ids)
    configuration = {
        "fits": fit_record["fits"],
        "pooled": is_pooled,
        "jax_enable_x64": enable_x64,
        "jaxcmr_version": jaxcmr.__version__,
        "model_factory": fit_record["model_factory"],
        "components": fit_record["components"],
        "simulation_function": fit_record["simulation_function"],
        "data_path": data_source,
        "selected_trial_indices": np.flatnonzero(np.asarray(selected_trials)).tolist(),
        "embedding_path": fit_record.get("embedding_path", ""),
        "emotion_feature_path": fit_record.get("emotion_feature_path", ""),
        "feature_column": fit_record.get("feature_column", 6),
        "concat_features": fit_record.get("concat_features", False),
        "seed": simulation_seed,
        "experiment_count": experiment_count,
    }

    for key in ("embedding_path", "emotion_feature_path"):
        if configuration[key]:
            feature_path = resolve_project_path(configuration[key], root_path)
            configuration[key] = (feature_path.relative_to(root_path).as_posix()
                          if feature_path.is_relative_to(root_path) else str(feature_path))
    simulation_inputs[model_name] = {
        "model_factory": model_factory,
        "features": features,
        "parameters": subject_parameters,
        "trial_mask": selected_trials,
        "configuration": configuration,
    }
13 — Generate or reuse matching responses and save them 
simulations = {}
for model_name, prepared in simulation_inputs.items():
    model_factory = prepared["model_factory"]
    features = prepared["features"]
    subject_parameters = prepared["parameters"]
    selected_trials = prepared["trial_mask"]
    configuration = prepared["configuration"]
    simulation_path = simulation_paths[model_name]
    simulated = None
    if not redo_sims:
        simulated = load_matching_simulation(simulation_path, configuration)
    if simulated is None:
        simulated = simulate_dataset(
            model_factory,
            data,
            features,
            subject_parameters,
            selected_trials,
            experiment_count=experiment_count,
            rng=jax.random.PRNGKey(simulation_seed),
            simulate_trial_fn=import_from_string(configuration["simulation_function"]),
        )
        simulation_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        save_dict_to_hdf5(simulated, str(simulation_path))
        simulation_path.with_suffix(".json").write_text(
            json.dumps(
                {
                    **configuration,
                    "jaxcmr_version": jaxcmr.__version__,
                    "jax_version": jax.__version__,
                },
                indent=2,
            )
            + "\n"
        )
        print("Saved responses:", simulation_path)
    else:
        print("Loaded matching responses:", simulation_path)
    if filter_repeated_recalls:
        simulated = simulated.copy()
        simulated["recalls"] = repetition.filter_repeated_recalls(simulated["recalls"])
    simulations[model_name] = simulated
print(
    "simulation_paths =",
    {model_name: str(path) for model_name, path in simulation_paths.items()},
)

Inspect behavioral summaries

The analysis configurations choose the behavioral comparisons. Their selection rules can differ from the fitting selection, so check which lists enter each display. Confidence intervals summarize participants; simulation repetitions are not additional independent participants.

Keep response files for subsequent analysis. You can inspect another behavior with an analysis template without simulating again.

14 — Prepare configured model and observation comparisons 
comparison_groups = []
if (
    redo_figures
    and comparison_analysis_configs
    and any(not np.array_equal(mask, comparison_mask) for mask in selections.values())
):
    raise ValueError(
        "Shared comparison figures need matching selections; use separate jobs or disable comparison_analysis_configs."
    )

if redo_figures and simulations:
    observed = data.copy()
    if filter_repeated_recalls:
        observed["recalls"] = repetition.filter_repeated_recalls(observed["recalls"])
    datasets = [observed, *simulations.values()]
    names = ["Observed", *[display_labels[name] for name in simulations]]
    comparison_groups.append(
        {
            "analyses": comparison_analysis_configs,
            "datasets": datasets,
            "labels": names,
            "base_masks": [comparison_mask, *[None for _ in simulations]],
            "suffix": "",
        }
    )
    for dataset_index, (dataset, label) in enumerate(zip(datasets, names)):
        comparison_groups.append(
            {
                "analyses": single_analysis_configs,
                "datasets": [dataset],
                "labels": [label],
                "base_masks": [comparison_mask if dataset_index == 0 else None],
                "suffix": f"_single_{dataset_index}",
            }
        )
Code 
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
#| code-summary: "15 — Plot and save the configured benchmarks"

for group in comparison_groups:
    panel_data = group["datasets"]
    analysis_configs = group["analyses"]
    curve_labels = group["labels"]
    base_masks = group["base_masks"]
    for figure, figure_suffix in iter_analysis_figures(
        panel_data,
        analysis_configs,
        curve_labels,
        base_masks=base_masks,
        trial_query=analysis_trial_query,
        confidence_level=confidence_level,
        figure_size=figure_size,
        suffix=group["suffix"],
        bootstrap_seed=plot_seed,
    ):
        if figure_str:
            save_figure(
                str(figure_dir),
                figure_str,
                suffix=figure_suffix,
                formats=figure_formats,
                figure=figure,
            )
        else:
            figure.tight_layout()
        plt.show()

Reuse the results

Use the printed simulation_paths as data_paths in the analysis templates, with matching labels. Each HDF5 file has a JSON file of simulation settings; retain both if you will reuse responses or run model comparison. With explicit simulation_dir, responses may be outside output_dir.

For a new experiment or model, supply compatible observations and fit records, change the seed or repetitions as needed, and select a distinct destination.

The Templates overview describes how saved products connect.
